title: Three Weeks and One Short Bandage
subtitle: 身体健康 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 身体健康（人与自我·身体部位与健康）
meta: 主题语境：身体健康（人与自我·身体部位与健康）　|　核心词汇：foot　|　正文 343 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 foot 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1969 the nurse ① bandaged a foot that no doctor in the ward would have measured, and she said the bandaging was the whole of the morning. The ② foot, meaning the sole itself and not the leg, ran three weeks and stayed unmeasured in the book; a foot, she said, is the only thing in a ward that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ injured foot in that ward had the same short bandage beside it, and the ④ foot at the far bed, meaning the one they kept for the child and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A foot, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the nurse said the measuring is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the foot was the whole of the matter, meaning the measure and not the sole. The ⑥ foot, meaning the measure and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; foot, he said, is either something you bandage or the only word that means both a sole and a measure. He said the measure is the part they remember.

By 1976 the ⑦ foot had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short bandage. The ⑧ foot of the whole thing, the nurse wrote in May, was one ward and three weeks of measuring; foot, she said, is either the one at the far bed or the reason you learned to measure. She said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ foot I remember is the one measured in the plan, which closed in 1978 and is still described as the quietest in the ward. A ⑩ foot, my mother said in 1980, is the only one that improves by being measured; every foot, she said, is a measure that has agreed to look like a sole. She said the measure was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 脚；足（指病房里每一只旁边的那一只）
B. n. 脚（指那一只本身，与腿相对）
C. 固定搭配：bandage a foot 包扎一只脚
D. n. 脚（指留给孩子的那一只）
E. n. 脚（抽象总称，指一间病房的包扎之事）
F. n. 脚（指计划里写到、被量过的那一只）
G. n. 英尺（长度单位，指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）
H. n. 英尺（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）

answers.why: bandage a foot 意为“包扎一只脚”，1969 年那位护士包扎了一只病房里没有一位医生肯量过的脚。
foot 意为“脚”，指那一只本身而不是腿，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被量过。
foot 意为“脚”，指病房里每一只旁边的那一只，每一只旁边都有同一条短短的绷带。
foot 意为“脚”，指留给孩子的那一只，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
foot 意为“英尺”，指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西，叔叔说这一英尺就是那件事的全部。
foot 意为“英尺”，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西而不是那一只脚，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
foot 意为“脚”，指计划里写到、被量过的那一只，到 1976 年这一只成了计划里的一行。
foot 意为“脚”，护士五月写道，整件事的包扎之事是一间病房和三个星期的量过。
foot 意为“脚”，我记得的是计划里量过的那一只，1978 年结束了，至今仍被说成病房里最安静的一只。
foot 为抽象总称，母亲 1980 年说，一只脚是唯一会因为被好好量过而变得更好的东西。
